name: Intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) GABAergic neuron
anatomy_mentioned: intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) of the lateral geniculate complex
thin flat leaflet between dorsal and ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
historically a subdivision of the ventrolateral geniculate nucleus (VLG)
medial vLGN of cat proposed as IGL homologue
pregeniculate nucleus of primates proposed as IGL homologue
morphology_summary: Not described at single-cell level. Population is a bilateral, retinorecipient leaflet; outputs include the geniculohypothalamic tract to the SCN (NPY cells) and the geniculo-geniculate tract to the contralateral IGL (ENK cells).
ephys_summary: Network shows infra-slow / ultradian oscillations that depend on retinal drive and GABA_A signalling; population splits into an I_T-expressing (non-NPY/ENK) group and an I_A-expressing (NPY) group. Depolarised by orexin A via non-selective cation channels; hyperpolarised by met-enkephalin via mu-opioid receptors.
subtypes_noted: Two main peptide/projection classes, NPY+ (SCN-projecting) and ENK+ (contralateral IGL-projecting) (Blasiak et al., 2013; Chrobok et al., 2016; Palus et al., 2017). A third group with unknown transmitter content (Blasiak et al._1, 2013, citing Moore & Card 1994). Three juxtacellularly defined light-response classes in IGL/VLG, Type I NPY-, Type II strong somatic NPY, Type III patchy/internalised NPY (Thankachan et al., 2005). Retained as notes, not nodes.

relation_to_existing.justification: The existing node pools LGv and IGL GABAergic neurons; this node restricts to the IGL, which the report describes as a mainly or wholly GABAergic leaflet historically treated as a subdivision of the VLG (Chrobok et al., 2016; Palus et al., 2015).

name: Intergeniculate leaflet NPY-positive geniculohypothalamic neuron
anatomy_mentioned: suprachiasmatic nucleus (axon terminals, via geniculohypothalamic tract)
cat medial vLGN (SCN-projecting, NPY-immunoreactive processes; proposed homologue)
morphology_summary: Projection neuron forming the geniculohypothalamic tract; NPY-positive fibres abundant in the SCN. No somatodendritic description.
ephys_summary: All NPY+ neurons tested show a marked A-type K+ current (I_A) (Chrobok et al., 2016). SCN-projecting neurons fire at low, irregular rates in light and most increase firing in darkness (Blasiak et al., 2013). Excited by relaxin-3 (R3/I5) stimulation (Blasiak et al._1, 2013). Hyperpolarised by met-enkephalin (Palus et al., 2017).
subtypes_noted: Thankachan et al., 2005: Type II IGL/VLG neurons (strong somatic NPY; suppression, complex or no response to illumination) likely correspond to this class; Type III neurons with patchy/internalised NPY are interpreted as NPY recipients, not NPY producers, so must not be assigned here on NPY immunolabel alone.

relation_to_existing.justification: NPY-synthesising neurons are one of the two main GABAergic subpopulations of the IGL (Blasiak et al., 2013; Chrobok et al., 2016; Palus et al., 2017).

name: Intergeniculate leaflet enkephalinergic geniculo-geniculate neuron
anatomy_mentioned: contralateral intergeniculate leaflet (axon terminals, via geniculo-geniculate tract)
morphology_summary: Projection neuron forming the geniculo-geniculate tract to the contralateral IGL; receives direct retinal innervation; proposed to act as a local interneuron-like inhibitory element on itself and on NPY cells, ipsi- and contralaterally. No somatodendritic description.
ephys_summary: T-type Ca2+ current (I_T) in neurons that do not synthesise NPY (Chrobok et al., 2016). In vivo, all contralateral-IGL-projecting neurons show infra-slow (<0.1 Hz) oscillatory bursting, sustained in light and reduced in darkness (Blasiak et al., 2013; Chrobok et al., 2017). Hyperpolarised by met-enkephalin via mu-opioid receptors (Palus et al., 2017).
subtypes_noted: Report notes no finer molecular subdivision within ENK class. ENK identity is partly inferred: Chrobok et al., 2016 define the I_T group as 'neurons that do not synthesise NPY'; later papers equate it with ENK cells; ISO cells are described as 'putatively enkephalinergic' (Chrobok et al., 2017).

relation_to_existing.justification: Enkephalinergic cells are the second main GABAergic subpopulation of the IGL, projecting to the contralateral IGL (Blasiak et al., 2013; Palus et al., 2017; Palus-Chramiec et al., 2019).
